turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: My concerns are not solely about the Muslim preachers, Sandip. They are about the unrest you actively cultivate amongst those who depend on my protection. I will not tolerate the exploitation of my tenants, regardless of your motivations.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Exploitation, you say? A rather dramatic term, wouldn't you agree, Nikhil? It's always so gratifying to witness the lengths to which one must go to appear righteous, even when the truth – the *real* truth – lies elsewhere, buried beneath layers of self-importance and inherited privilege.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Such strong words, Nikhil, though I confess, I find myself wondering... what *is* the true measure of righteousness in these times?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your attempts at veiled insults are tiresome, Sandip. I am not concerned with your assessment of my character, nor with your theatrical pronouncements about truth. My focus remains on maintaining order and ensuring the well-being of those under my care.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Maintaining order, you say? A commendable aspiration, Nikhil, though history is replete with examples of those who sought order and ultimately delivered only tyranny. Tell me, does the shepherd truly protect his flock, or merely fatten them for the slaughter?

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: A shepherd's duty is surely to protect, Sandip, though perhaps the definition of 'protection' itself is open to interpretation. Does it involve shielding them from hardship, or simply from discomfort?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your analogies are needlessly provocative, Sandip, and demonstrate a fundamental misunderstanding of my intentions. I strive for fairness, not tyranny, and I find your constant attempts to cast me in a negative light both unproductive and tiresome. Let us speak plainly: if you have concerns regarding my conduct, present them directly, rather than resorting to these oblique and inflammatory comparisons.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Fairness, you claim? A noble sentiment, Nikhil, much like the pronouncements of Pilate before he washed his hands of the consequences. Tell me, when the storm clouds gather and the faithful seek shelter, will your 'fairness' be enough to shield them, or will you simply point to the heavens and declare it is their own fault for being exposed?

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: The heavens are vast, Sandip, and their judgments often inscrutable. Perhaps it is not a matter of fault, but of perspective – of understanding the forces at play and adapting to their inevitable sway.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Perspective, you say, Bimala? A fascinating notion, though I find it often serves as a convenient veil for inaction. Tell me, Nikhil, when those 'forces' you speak of – the whispers of dissent, the fervor of righteous indignation – begin to coalesce, will your perspective allow you to see the danger, or will you be too busy admiring the shifting patterns of the sky?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your attempts at dramatic pronouncements, Sandip, are tiresome and ultimately reveal a lack of substance. I am not naive to the currents of unrest, and I am not blind to the concerns of my tenants. However, I will not be intimidated by veiled threats or theatrical pronouncements of doom.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Ah, Nikhil, so easily dismissed, so quick to declare a lack of substance. Tell me, does the ostrich bury its head in the sand because it fears the storm, or because it believes the storm cannot see it? I merely offer observations, my dear fellow; consider them as…warnings, perhaps, delivered in the manner most likely to penetrate a thick skull.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your analogies are needlessly elaborate, Sandip, and betray a desire for attention rather than genuine concern. I am fully aware of the anxieties within the community, and I am actively working to address them through established channels, not through provocative rhetoric. If you possess information regarding specific threats, I urge you to present them directly, rather than cloaking them in such theatrics.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Established channels, you say? How reassuringly… conventional. But sometimes, Nikhil, the established channels are merely conduits for the very forces one seeks to control. I trust you haven’t entirely forgotten the tales of Icarus, did you, my friend? He, too, believed in his own methods.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your allusions to mythology are a distraction from the matter at hand, Sandip. I am not interested in fanciful comparisons, but in demonstrable facts. If you have evidence of wrongdoing within my estate or threats against my family, I expect you to present it with clarity and without resorting to such elaborate and frankly, tiresome displays.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: The air feels…charged, doesn't it? Perhaps, Nikhil, a little less emphasis on pronouncements and a little more on understanding what truly troubles people would serve us all better.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Sandip, your persistent attempts to draw parallels between my actions and mythological failures are unproductive and, I suspect, intended to unsettle. I am not blind to the underlying currents of unrest, but I will not be swayed by theatrical pronouncements or veiled accusations. State your concerns plainly, or leave.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Ah, demonstrable facts, are we clinging to such rigid principles, Nikhil? It’s a pity, really, because the most potent truths often reside just beyond the grasp of empirical observation – like the subtle tremor before an earthquake, or the quiet murmurings of discontent that precede a storm. I merely offer a different lens through which to view these currents, a lens perhaps less comfortable than your own, but no less revealing.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: A storm, you say? I find myself wondering, Sandip, if it is the storm we should fear, or the shadows it casts. Perhaps it is not so much the tremor, but what we choose to build upon it that determines our fate.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Bimala, you possess a remarkable talent for metaphor, truly. But tell me, does pondering shadows truly offer solace when the roof itself is about to collapse? I find it rather… convenient, wouldn’t you agree, Nikhil, that we concern ourselves with the aesthetics of impending ruin?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I say, Nikhil, don't you keep Browning among your books here? I was just telling Queen Bee of our college club. Do you remember that contest of ours over the translation of those lines from Browning? You don't?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I managed to get together the words to render it into Bengali, somehow, but the result was hardly likely to be a 'joy forever' to the people of Bengal. I really did think at one time that I was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence was kind enough to save me from that disaster. Do you remember old Dakshina? If he had not become a Salt Inspector, he would have been a poet. I remember his rendering to this day ...

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: No, Queen Bee, it is no use rummaging those bookshelves. Nikhil has ceased to read poetry since his marriage--perhaps he has no further need for it. But I suppose 'the fever fit of poesy', as the Sanskrit has it, is about to attack me again.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I have come to give you a warning, Sandip.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: About the fever fit of poesy?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: For some time, Mahomedan preachers have been about stirring up the local Mussulmans. They are all wild with you, and may attack you any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Are you come to advise flight?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Had these estates been mine, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for me. If, instead of trying to frighten me, you give them a taste of your intimidation, that would be worthier both of you and me. Do you know that your weakness is weakening your neighbouring zamindars also?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I did not offer you my advice, Sandip. I wish you, too, would refrain from giving me yours. Besides, it is useless. And there is another thing I want to tell you. You and your followers have been secretly worrying and oppressing my tenantry. I cannot allow that any longer. So I must ask you to leave my territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: For fear of the Mussulmans, or is there any other fear you have to threaten me with?
